title: Tensor core inefficiency detection - Nsight sweep & timeline notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an ad-hoc Nsight/CUDA-graph profiling sweep focused on cases where tensor cores show unexpectedly low utilization despite high SM utilization and apparent arithmetic intensity. The goal is to collect reproducible traces, document hypotheses, and propose small runtime mitigations to improve end-to-end token latency for medium-length contexts (512-1k tokens).

Background & motivation:
- Several production traces from Dedicated clusters (p100->a100-like runs) showed SM active cycles high (~70-85%) but tensor core activity reported by Nsight Compute is surprisingly low (~20-35%) on kernels we expect to be matmul-heavy.
- Impact: more FP ops executed on scalar paths or lower-throughput FMAs, increasing per-token latency and raising per-token GPU cost.
- Candidate root causes: suboptimal tile shapes, non-FP16 paths (reduced mixed precision usage), kernel fusion that breaks tensorization patterns, misaligned input shapes, or frequent small-kernel launches that prevent tensor-core batching.

Reproduction plan (machines / env):
- HW: internal dev node with A100-40GB (cuda 12.1 toolkit), identical runtime build used on Dedicated.
- Docker: runtime:release-2026-06 (image tag used for the Dedicated pool in eu-west).
- Dataset: synthetic transformer inputs with lengths [128, 512, 1024]; token batch sizes [1, 2, 8, 16]; tests both with KV caching cold and warm states.
- Model: quantized fp16 variant of our 13B transformer (same compile profile used in production).
- Nsight tools: nsight-compute 2025.3 and nsight-systems 2025.2 for timeline captures.

Nsight capture config (CLI examples):
- timeline capture with syscalls & cuda api:
  nsys profile --output=nsys/tensor-ineff-512b1 --sample=none --cpuctxsw --trace=cuda,nvtx --force-overwrite --duration-ms=0 --target-processes=all --capture-range=auto -- /bin/bash -c "./run_inference --len 512 --batch 1"

- per-kernel detail capture (selective kernels to keep trace size small):
  ncu --metrics gld_throughput,gst_throughput,dram_read_throughput,sm_efficiency,achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency, tensor_core_utilization --target-processes=all --set=full --launch-skip 0 --launch-count 500 --output ncu/tensor-512-b1 ./run_inference --len 512 --batch 1

Important measurement notes:
- Use NVTX ranges around high-level runtime operations (compile, compile-kernel, run, kv-lookup, prefix-cache-hit) to connect kernel launches to logical stages.
- Capture both cold-start (clear caches) and warmed KV cache to see differences in kernel shapes and number of launches.
- Make sure to pin CPU affinity to avoid preemption affecting timeline clarity.

Key observations (sampled from 2026-07-15 runs):
- For len=512 batch=1 cold-run: SM efficiency ~78%, achieved_occupancy average ~0.61, tensor_core_utilization ~28%.
- For len=512 batch=8 warm-run: SM efficiency ~82%, achieved_occupancy ~0.67, tensor_core_utilization ~58% — tensor use improves when microbatching increases problem size, but still below theoretical expectation for fused matmuls.
- Kernel timeline shows many short (<120us) matmul-like kernels interleaved with small elementwise kernels and KV-copy kernels. Tensor core spikes coincide with the largest matmuls but many matmul-shaped kernels are too narrow (M or N dimension small) to trigger tensorization.
- Nsight shows a subset of kernels compiled with wmma intrinsics (expected), but many remaining matmul-path kernels compiled to non-tensor FMA loops, flagged by low l2 throughput and high register use.
- A surprising find: kernels that use int8 reduction for attention (fast path) had near-zero tensor core usage (as expected), but were invoked more often than anticipated in the warm KV scenario due to an optimization in compile profile that split attention into smaller int8-friendly tiles for memory reasons.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Tile shapes produced by the compiler/runtime for medium sequence lengths produce small K or N dims that fall below the tensor core threshold.
2) Kernel fusion decisions in the runtime produce many small kernels to improve memory locality but break up large matmuls into numerous small ones, reducing tensorization opportunities.
3) Mixed precision lowering sometimes falls back to FP32 loops for borderline numerics (safety heuristics), preventing tensor core usage.
4) CUDA graph submission ordering and stream choreography result in many small kernel launches that cannot be coalesced into larger CUDA Graph nodes, hurting tensor core amortization.

Quick experiments run to test hypotheses:
- Forced tile remap: re-run compile with a hacked tiling config that forces larger MxN tiles for the attention matmul when len >= 256. Result: tensor_core_utilization on the critical kernel rose from 28% -> ~61% at len=512, batch=1. End-to-end token latency decreased ~8-12% on the hot path.
- Fusion off: disable one fusion pass that collapses attention+project into a single kernel. Surprisingly, end-to-end latency increased slightly while tensor core utilization improved for matmul kernels. Explanation: fusion had improved memory locality but created shapes that prevented tensorization. Net effect depends on workload distribution.
- Graph coalescing: group sequential small kernels into a single cudaGraph node (experimental patch). This reduced kernel launch overhead but did not materially change tensor_core_utilization unless the graph node also allowed larger tiled matmuls.

Detailed trace note (example):
- Trace segment 0x7f8a (warm run len=512 batch=1):
  - NVTX: attention_forward_start -> attention_matmul_a (kernel K1, 98us) -> eltwise_relu (K2, 18us) -> attention_matmul_b (K3, 112us) -> kv_copy (K4, 32us)
  - K1 metrics: achieved_occupancy=0.59, sm_efficiency=0.76, tensor_core_utilization=22%, l2_read_throughput low
  - K3 metrics: achieved_occupancy=0.62, sm_efficiency=0.80, tensor_core_utilization=65%, l2_read_throughput high
  Interpretation: K1 and K3 are similar op types but divergent shapes or compiler lowering. K3 uses a tile shape that maps well to wmma kernels.

Practical mitigations to try in order (short-term -> medium-term):
- Short-term: add a compile-time tiling guard that prefers larger M/N tiles for sequence lengths >=256. This is a cheap toggle and we can A/B it on a small Dedicated shard.
- Short-term: tweak the safety threshold for fp16 fallback to be more permissive for common workloads; add a per-model override toggle while we collect regression metrics.
- Medium-term: improve fusion heuristics to avoid fusing in a way that reduces tensorization opportunities; instead allow an alternate fusion schedule that preserves matmul shape.
- Medium-term: enhance CUDA-graph coalescing to merge sequential matmul kernels into a single larger matmul when possible, possibly by emitting a single fused kernel that preserves tile sizes.
- Long-term: extend kernel autotuner to profile tensor core efficiency metric directly and prefer tilings that maximize tensor_core_utilization subject to latency constraints.

Open action items / experiments to follow up:
- Run an A/B on dedicated shard with forced-large-tiling flag enabled for 48 hours: monitor token latency, latency p95/p99, cost per token. Owner: Evan. Jira: INF-3421.
- Add NSIGHT CI job that captures the same metrics and uploads condensed csvs so we can track tensor_core_utilization across releases. Owner: Liang. PR: runtime/pull/784.
- Investigate one fused kernel that consistently compiles to non-wmma path; dump lowering IR and share with compiler team for advice. Owner: Marta.
- Create a small unit test / microbenchmark that reproduces the small-tile behavior deterministically so we can test autotuner changes. Owner: Priya.

Notes on measurement pitfalls:
- Nsight sampling overhead can perturb short kernels; prefer aggregated counters across many iterations.
- Achieved_occupancy calculation depends on active threads per block versus max, but registers and shared mem can artificially cap achievable occupancy; look at register usage metric as cross-check.
- Tensor_core_utilization reported by some Nsight metric sets is an aggregate and can be misleading when multiple concurrent kernels run; correlate with timeline-level GPU timeline to avoid mis-attributing activity.

Summary (one-liner):
Many low-tensor-core cases are caused not by hardware limits but by tile shapes and runtime fusion choices that fragment matmuls. Quick wins: force larger tile sizes for medium-length contexts and add a CI Nsight sweep to alert regressions.

Appendix - commands & snippets:
- dump single kernel metadata with ncu:
  ncu --target-processes=all --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency,tensor_core_utilization,sm_active_cycles --kernel-id <id> --output kernel-metadata ./run_inference --len 512 --batch 1

- lightweight timeline capture for production reproduction:
  nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys_short --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none --nvtx-emit -- ./run_inference --len 512 --batch 1 --iterations 100

End of note.
